title: Verifier characterization with success thresholds
statement: For a function $p\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Q}$ and a Boolean language $L$, there are a verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$ such that the verifier has polynomial-time efficiency, and for every Boolean input $x$, if $x\in L$ then the probability over random strings $r$ of $M(x,r)=\mathrm{true}$ is at least $p(|x|)$, while if $x\notin L$ then the probability of $M(x,r)=\mathrm{false}$ is at least $p(|x|)$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$
Completeness probability at least $p(|x|)$ for members
Soundness probability at least $p(|x|)$ for nonmembers
